prompt:
Research what the Python Software Foundation or the CPython developers have officially said about the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build. Cite the PEP or documentation page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Based on the provided web search results, here is what the Python Software Foundation and CPython developers have officially stated about the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build.

The primary sources for official statements are PEP 703, PEP 779, and the Python 3.14.5 documentation.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "The changes to make CPython thread-safe without the GIL increase execution overhead for `--disable-gil` builds." | CLAIM: Acknowledges that the free-threaded build has inherent execution overhead.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "The performance impact is different for programs that use only a single thread compared to programs that use multiple threads..." | CLAIM: The performance impact varies based on whether the program uses a single thread or multiple threads.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "One thread | 6% | 5%" | CLAIM: Provides specific measured overhead for single-threaded programs on different CPU architectures.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "Multiple threads | 8% | 7%" | CLAIM: Provides specific measured overhead for multi-threaded programs on different CPU architectures.
SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "On the pyperformance benchmark suite, the average overhead ranges from about 1% on macOS aarch64 to 8% on x86-64 Linux systems." | CLAIM: Confirms the performance overhead and provides a range across different operating systems and architectures.
SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075?u=hugovk | QUOTE: "At this point we’re expecting a (worst case) performance penalty of 10-15%." | CLAIM: The Steering Council's expectation for a worst-case performance penalty.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "The performance penalty on linear performance... is currently around 10% (except on macOS, where it’s more like 3%)." | CLAIM: Provides a current estimate of the performance penalty for the free-threaded build.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "we propose 15% as a hard performance target [for phase II]." | CLAIM: Proposes a specific, acceptable performance target for the officially supported free-threaded build.
SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "The free-threaded build will typically use more memory compared to the default build." | CLAIM: Acknowledges that the free-threaded build has higher memory usage.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "free-threaded Python currently sees about 15-20% higher memory use (geometric mean, as measured by pyperformance)." | CLAIM: Quantifies the increased memory usage of the free-threaded build.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "we propose a target of 20% (geometric mean, as measured by pyperformance) for phase II." | CLAIM: Proposes a specific, acceptable memory usage target for the officially supported free-threaded build.
SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "Note that this PEP would not affect the performance of the default (non `--disable-gil`) builds of CPython." | CLAIM: States that the performance of the standard GIL-enabled build is unaffected by the development of the free-threaded build.
